consensus_findings.description: Critical: Spec contract mismatch between build_atlas.py --tree footer format and explain-code grounding disclosure line.
Nit: Work package definitions in work-packages.yaml omit task numbers added in tasks.md across all three packages.
Nit: Verification step in wp-atlas-tree writes to hardcoded shared temporary file paths in /tmp.
Nit: wp-integration verification steps in work-packages.yaml omit install manifest check and tree determinism verification.
Nit: tiny_graph fixture in codebase-atlas conftest.py contains no call cycles for task 1.1 cycle assertion.
FYI: Root line formatting for module targets is underspecified.
Optional: Disclosure line requirement applies to all replies, but non-call-tree forms are inherently ungrounded.
The frontmatter decoupled testing strategy cleanly handles in-flight migration.

Command injection risk in --tree target argument: The skill shells out to `build_atlas.py --tree <target>` where <target> comes from user questions. The spec says target resolves as 'exact node id, then unique symbol name, then module file path or basename' but no input sanitization or validation is specified. A user could inject shell metacharacters via a crafted symbol name or file path.

Path traversal when reading source files directly: The spec states 'the skill SHALL read source directly and label the sketch unverified' when graph is stale/absent, but specifies no path validation. A user asking about a symbol in '../../etc/passwd' could cause arbitrary file reads outside the repository.

Tight coupling between parallel work packages: wp-skill denies 'skills/codebase-atlas/**' but its grounding reference (references/grounding.md) must document the --tree contract (D3/D4/D5). The design explicitly says 'the grounding reference documents the --tree contract from design D3 rather than importing the implementation.' This creates a manual sync burden - if atlas implementation changes, skill documentation drifts with no automated detection.

Ambiguous phrase 'nodes that export returns' in grounding spec: The skill-workflow spec says 'SHALL build the call tree only from nodes that export returns.' This is undefined - could mean functions with return statements, nodes returned by --tree, or something else. Implementation will be inconsistent.

Exit code 2 ambiguity breaks fallback logic: Exit code 2 means both 'target not found' AND 'ambiguous target (multiple matches)'. The skill-workflow spec says 'WHEN build_atlas.py --tree exits 2 (target not found) ... fall back to source reading'. But for ambiguous matches, the symbol EXISTS in the graph - falling back to source reading is wrong; the skill should ask for clarification.

Multi-language disclosure footer format unspecified: The spec says footer has 'per language present' but doesn't define the exact format (comma? slash? newline?). Design shows 'python 14% / sql 37% covered' with slashes but spec uses ellipsis. The skill must copy this exactly for the disclosure line - format mismatch will cause test failures.

No machine-readable contract for --tree output or disclosure line: The contracts/README.md explicitly states 'Consuming skills treat a contracts/ directory containing only this README as no contracts applicable.' The two text-level contracts (--tree output format, disclosure line) have no schema validation. Behavioral tests only check string presence, not format correctness.

Cycle detection underspecified for --direction in/both: Spec says 'A node already printed on the current path is emitted once with suffix (cycle) and not expanded.' For --direction in (callers), the graph edges are reversed. Cycle detection must work on the traversed direction, but spec doesn't clarify if cycles are detected in directed or undirected sense.

Hard-coded hop limit of 4 with no extensibility: Maximum hops clamped at 4 to match atlas page slider. This UX coupling means deep call chains (>4 hops) cannot be explored via --tree even if user explicitly requests more. The stderr note on clamping is insufficient - user has no way to override.

No observability requirements for new CLI flag or skill: NFR table covers coverage honesty, determinism, operability, context cost, compatibility, portability - but no logging, tracing, or metrics for --tree invocations or explain-code skill usage. In production, failures will be invisible.

Inconsistent helper module name across documents: Proposal.md says 'a tree.py helper module' but tasks.md (1.2) and design.md (D8) correctly name it 'atlas_tree.py' to satisfy collect-uncollected-skill-tests. Proposal should be updated for consistency.

NFR timing target based on unverified graph data: Proposal states 'Operability: --tree wall time on the committed graph (1,903 nodes / 1,199 edges) ≤ 2s' but proposal.md Impact section admits 'architecture refresh failed with three validator errors during planning and parallel_zones.json is absent, so the node/edge counts above come from the committed architecture.summary.json and are unverified against the current tree.' The 2s target may be unrealistic for actual graph size.

Skill base directory path construction could allow directory traversal: Skill constructs script paths as '<skill-base-dir>/../refresh-architecture/scripts/run_architecture.py'. If skill-base-dir is manipulated (symlinks, bind mounts), this could escape the skills directory. The skill system should validate skill-base-dir is within expected root.

Work package deny rules complicate integration merge: wp-atlas-tree denies 'skills/explain-code/**' and wp-skill denies 'skills/codebase-atlas/**'. Task 3.1 says 'Merge the wp-atlas-tree and wp-skill package branches ... resolving any overlap in skills/install-manifest.json'. But both packages modify install-manifest.json (wp-atlas-tree doesn't list it in write_allow but wp-skill does). The deny rules may prevent proper conflict resolution during merge.

Sorting locale not specified for deterministic output: Spec says 'children SHALL be sorted by name then id' and 'Output SHALL be byte-identical across runs'. But string sorting is locale-dependent (LC_COLLATE). Different CI environments may produce different byte output for non-ASCII symbol names.
